text: The Sennet Lighthouse was decommissioned in 1987, according to records released Tuesday by the Calder Port Authority. The 112-year-old beacon on Greyhook Point was shut down after coastal navigation equipment made the tower redundant, and its Fresnel lens was later moved to the Harbour Maritime Museum. Port historian Elin Voss said the agency has since maintained the site as a protected landmark. “The lighthouse served generations of mariners, but it has not guided ships since 1987,” Voss said. Officials said minor repair work is scheduled next month to stabilize the masonry before the winter storm season. The tower remains closed to the public except during supervised heritage tours.
